summary: Benedetta Lomi works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from SOAS University of London, later teaching at the University of Virginia around 2014 to 2019 and holding a post at the University of Bristol around 2019.

Benimadhab Barua (1888–1948) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied across numerous institutions, earning degrees from Krishnath College, Presidency University, University of Calcutta, and University of London. He was a lecturer and later professor at the University of Calcutta.

Sinologist and historian Benjamin A. Elman completed his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Nathan Sivin and Susan Naquin. He taught at UCLA (1986–2002) and Princeton University, where he directed the East Asian Studies Program in 2002.

Benjamin Bogin specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan, studying under Janet Gyatso, Gareth Sparham, and doctoral supervisor Donald S. Lopez Jr.

Benjamin Brose is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his PhD from Stanford under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure. Around 2009 to 2016, he served as assistant professor of Chinese Buddhism at the University of Michigan.
Benjamin W. Fortson IV is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Yale University and Harvard University. Around 2004, he held a post at the University of Michigan.

Benjamin Wood specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Toronto under doctoral supervisor Frances Garrett, and studied under Shayne Clarke, Thupten Champa, and traditional teacher Khenpo Kunga Sherab.

Benkyo Shiio (1876–1971) was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He taught Buddhism at several universities, headed Taisho University (1926) and Tokai Gakuen Women's College (1963), and directed the Sanko institutions.

Benoytosh Bhattacharyya (1897–1964) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from the University of Calcutta and the University of Dhaka. In 1927, he became Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara.

Benoît Vermander specializes in Sinology and religious studies. He earned degrees from Yale, Sciences Po, Fu Jen Catholic University, and Centre Sèvres, and served as Academic Director at the Taipei Ricci Institute before joining Fudan University in 2009.

Bernard Faure specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He earned a Doctorat d'État at the University of Paris, studied under Paul Demiéville and Seizan Yanagida, and held professorships at Cornell, Stanford, and Columbia University.

Bernard Frank (1927–1996) was a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied under Rolf A. Stein. He headed the Maison Franco-Japonaise (~1972–1974) and held the chair of Civilisation japonaise at the Collège de France (1979–1996).

Bernard Williams (1929–2003) was a philosopher who studied at Balliol College, Oxford. He held academic posts at University College London from around 1959 to 1964 and at the University of California, Berkeley from around 1988 to 2003.
Bernd Schneidmüller is a historian who held posts at the University of Oldenburg from around 1987 to 1992 and at Heidelberg University around 2003.

Bernfried Schlerath (1924–2003) was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied under Paul Thieme and held posts at Goethe University Frankfurt, University of Marburg, and Free University of Berlin.
Bernhard Breloer (1894–1947) was an Indologist who succeeded Heinrich Lüders and held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin from around 1935 to 1945.

Bernhard Forssman is a linguist and scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg under Karl Hoffmann, later holding posts at the University of Marburg (1968–1983) and Erlangen-Nürnberg (1983).

Bernhard Geiger (1881–1964) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Vienna, Heidelberg, Bonn, and Göttingen. He taught at the University of Vienna (~1909–1938), Asia Institute (1938–1951), and Columbia University (1951–1953).

Bernhard Hirzel (1807–1847) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Zurich, Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp, Göttingen, and Paris. He subsequently served as a reader, Dozent, and Privatdozent at the University of Zurich.

Bernhard Karlgren (1889–1978) was a Sinologist and linguist. He studied at Uppsala University (~1907–1915), where he also held a post (~1915–1918), before joining the University of Gothenburg (~1918–1939).
